title.fr: Les francophones, les Acadiens et les Québécois

text.en: A law says the federal government must offer its services in English and in French, everywhere in Canada.
text.fr: Une loi oblige le gouvernement fédéral à offrir ses services en anglais et en français, partout au Canada.

source.quote: The federal government is required by law to provide services throughout Canada in English and French.

verification.evidence: The federal government is required by law to provide services throughout Canada in English and French.

text.en: An Anglophone is a person whose first language is English. A Francophone is a person whose first language is French.
text.fr: Un anglophone est une personne dont la première langue est l'anglais. Un francophone est une personne dont la première langue est le français.

source.quote: Today, there are 18 million Anglophones—people who speak English as a first language—and seven million Francophones—people who speak French as their first language.

verification.evidence: Today, there are 18 million Anglophones—people who speak English as a first language—and seven million Francophones—people who speak French as their first language.

text.en: Outside Quebec, Ontario, New Brunswick and Manitoba are home to about one million Francophones. Smaller groups of Francophones live in the other provinces.
text.fr: Hors du Québec, l'Ontario, le Nouveau-Brunswick et le Manitoba comptent environ un million de francophones. De plus petits groupes de francophones vivent dans les autres provinces.

source.quote: one million Francophones live in Ontario, New Brunswick and Manitoba, with a smaller presence in other provinces.

verification.evidence: While the majority of Francophones live in the province of Quebec, one million Francophones live in Ontario, New Brunswick and Manitoba, with a smaller presence in other provinces.

text.en: The Acadians descend from French colonists. Those colonists started to settle in 1604 in the area that is now the Maritime provinces.
text.fr: Les Acadiens descendent de colons français. Ces colons ont commencé à s'établir en 1604 dans la région qui forme aujourd'hui les provinces maritimes.

source.quote: The Acadians are the descendants of French colonists who began settling in what are now the Maritime provinces in 1604.

verification.evidence: The Acadians are the descendants of French colonists who began settling in what are now the Maritime provinces in 1604.

text.en: From 1755 to 1763, while Britain and France were at war, more than two out of every three Acadians were forced out of their homeland.
text.fr: De 1755 à 1763, pendant que la Grande-Bretagne et la France étaient en guerre, plus de deux Acadiens sur trois ont été chassés de leur terre natale.

source.quote: Between 1755 and 1763, during the war between Britain and France, more than two-thirds of the Acadians were deported from their homeland.

verification.evidence: Between 1755 and 1763, during the war between Britain and France, more than two-thirds of the Acadians were deported from their homeland.

text.en: The deportation of the Acadians is known as the “Great Upheaval.” The Acadians lived through this hard time and kept their own identity.
text.fr: La déportation des Acadiens est connue sous le nom de « Grand Dérangement ». Les Acadiens ont survécu à cette dure épreuve et ont gardé leur identité propre.

source.quote: Despite this ordeal, known as the “Great Upheaval,” the Acadians survived and maintained their unique identity.

verification.evidence: Between 1755 and 1763, during the war between Britain and France, more than two-thirds of the Acadians were deported from their homeland. Despite this ordeal, known as the “Great Upheaval,” the Acadians survived and maintained their unique identity.

text.en: Acadian culture is thriving today. It is a lively part of French-speaking Canada.
text.fr: La culture acadienne est florissante aujourd'hui. Elle est une partie bien vivante du Canada francophone.

source.quote: Today, Acadian culture is flourishing and is a lively part of French-speaking Canada.

verification.evidence: Today, Acadian culture is flourishing and is a lively part of French-speaking Canada.

text.en: Most Quebecers descend from 8,500 French settlers who came in the 1600s and 1700s.
text.fr: La plupart des Québécois descendent de 8 500 colons français venus aux 17e et 18e siècles.

source.quote: Most are descendants of 8,500 French settlers from the 1600s and 1700s

verification.evidence: Quebecers are the people of Quebec, the vast majority French-speaking. Most are descendants of 8,500 French settlers from the 1600s and 1700s

text.en: In 2006, the House of Commons recognized that the Québécois are a nation inside a united Canada.
text.fr: En 2006, la Chambre des communes a reconnu que les Québécois forment une nation au sein d'un Canada uni.

source.quote: recognized in 2006 that the Quebecois form a nation within a united Canada.

verification.evidence: The House of Commons recognized in 2006 that the Quebecois form a nation within a united Canada.

text.en: About one million English-speaking Quebecers, called Anglo-Quebecers, live in Quebec. Their roots there go back 250 years, and they are a lively part of life in the province.
text.fr: Environ un million de Québécois d'expression anglaise, appelés Anglo-Québécois, vivent au Québec. Leurs racines y remontent à 250 ans, et ils sont une partie bien vivante de la province.

source.quote: One million Anglo-Quebecers have a heritage of 250 years and form a vibrant part of the Quebec fabric.

verification.evidence: One million Anglo-Quebecers have a heritage of 250 years and form a vibrant part of the Quebec fabric.
